blocks.content: This topic goes past the Architecture module's overview of filtering and scoring, into the actual three-stage pipeline, and one detail commonly missed: the scheduler never moves a Pod itself, it only ever writes a decision.

The scheduler's actual pipeline runs in three distinct stages: Filtering (eliminate nodes that genuinely cannot work), Scoring (rank the remaining candidates), and Binding (commit the final decision), each a real, separate phase.

blocks.alt: Three genuinely distinct stages, not one single, undifferentiated decision

blocks.content: Concrete filtering checks include whether a node has enough free resources to satisfy a Pod's requests (covered in the Namespaces & Resource Management module), whether it matches required node affinity rules, and whether any of its taints (covered in the Scheduling module) are untolerated.

blocks.alt: Real, specific checks, not an abstract, unnamed filtering step

blocks.content: Among the nodes that survive filtering, scoring considers things like spreading replicas evenly across nodes (recap the Pod Anti-Affinity topic's goal), and balancing overall resource usage, ranking viable candidates rather than treating them as equally good.

blocks.alt: Ranking genuinely viable candidates, not treating every surviving node as equally good

blocks.content: 4. Binding: a Decision, Not a Move
blocks.text: 4. Binding: a Decision, Not a Move

blocks.content: This is a genuinely important, often-missed detail: the scheduler does not itself move or start anything, the Bind step simply writes the scheduling decision back through the API server, exactly the pipeline covered in the API Server Request Flow topic, kubelet is what actually acts on it afterward.

blocks.alt: A written decision, not a direct action, the scheduler never touches the Pod itself

blocks.content: 5. The Scheduler Is Itself a Controller
blocks.text: 5. The Scheduler Is Itself a Controller

blocks.content: This entire pipeline is, itself, just another instance of the general control loop covered earlier in this module, watching for unscheduled Pods, computing a decision, and acting by writing it, the same fundamental pattern, applied to one specific, important job.

blocks.alt: Not a special, separate mechanism, just another controller, applying the same general pattern

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: The scheduler runs a real, three-stage pipeline, filtering (eliminate), scoring (rank), and binding (commit), not one undifferentiated decision.
It never moves a Pod itself, Binding only writes the decision via the API server, and the entire scheduler is itself just another instance of the general control loop.
